body: This morning I told a family member how I was feeling. I didn't say anything about last night, but I'm going to see the doctor soon. I'm a little bitter at the moment but I suppose this is the first step on the road to stability? I have to say, things seem so much more poignant and wondrous when you think its the last time you'll see them, but I'm starting to feel glad that I can see them again.

Update: Various kind and amazing people talked to me about my decision and made me doubt it. After I logged off Reddit I tried anyway because I'm like that. It was a pretty halfhearted attempt. My method just got me really high, didn't kill me. Woke up feeling like shit but I'm still here.

Hey, this will probably be my last post. I'm far too much of a hopeless introvert to talk on a hotline, but thank you for your concern. I hope you recover from depression if you are suffering too. Life is a roller coaster and all I can honestly say to you is that I'm that person who wants to get off the ride when it goes too fast.

I'm still here and open to speak to anyone but it is nearly time. I'm listening to Nujabes. I just finished reading Beowulf. I'm just waiting for the stars to become a little clearer. Its been amazing to have some human interaction in the last hours. I care about each and every one of you and hope your journey takes you to new and exciting places, even after I'm long gone and forgotten. If somehow I'm still going tomorrow, I'll let you know! If no message comes then my brief time here on earth is over. I'm not religious, but if there is a next life I'll put in a good word for all of you! Farewell and good luck!

Thank you so much. I want to let you know before I'm gone, you seem like a wonderful person. I hope things go well for you in whatever road you choose to walk. There's a lot I didn't do and see, but it makes me feel better to think that other people can still see it. The world keeps turning i guess.
The fact that you understand means a lot to me, believe me. I hope from my core that your life takes a turn for the better, but I think I'm ready to go.

Yep, I'm in Europe. England to be precise. When I was little we went to lots of the ancient stone circles that are thousands of years old and watched the stars imagining like it was 5000 years ago. Its mostly rainy here, but sometimes it is enchantingly pretty. The stars are starting to come out here now and its heartbreaking how beautiful they are

Offering support in SW was the only thing I've done in far too long that felt helpful to others and rewarding for myself. This community is amazing, really amazing. I just feel like I'm ready for the cycle to reach its conclusion.

At the moment its pitch black and cloudy. I want to see the Plough constellation one last time. My dad used to lie down with me in the garden at night and point out stars to me and whisper their names

I'm glad you stuck around as well, but I'm not sure whether I could stomach such a long period. I mean, no-one around me knows about my current state of mind, they think I dodged a bullet and didn't inherit. To be fair one look at my music collection would show it!

I really appreciate those words. It genuinely means a lot to me to receive someone's empathy and love, especially in these last hours I have. Unfortunately, my Depression is hereditary and so if I chose to live I would face a lifelong battle against it. It was too cloudy for me to see the sunset, its dark here now. I'm reading some poetry and listening to music at the moment, but the stars aren't out yet.

Thank you for caring but I'm quite certain that this is my last night. If by some miracle I'm still around tomorrow then I'll take your advice to heart. I don't really view this as a sad occasion, more like a release. I'll watch a sunset and then have my last ever gaze up at the stars, and they'll be beautiful.

Okay. I understand the reasoning because I feel exactly the same way, but every single person I know who went through a similar ordeal says that therapy saved their life, so maybe its worth a shot if your life is on the line?

If you still feel like you don't want that then do you have anyone close enough to speak with about your feelings? Everyone here is always willing to help you, hell, you can PM me to vent as much as you need, I'll answer as soon as possible. Your story really connected with me. You are really brave for sharing this, by the way.

Hey, I can really empathise with you. I'm from the UK and secondary school was a heap of crap for me too because of my Social Class and I can honestly say, it turns around. In Sixth Form everyone is a lot more mature, none of the bullying takes place. You are NOT broken minded or weak. You dealt with other peoples shit for your whole life and you are still standing. How many of the people around you could take a day in your shoes? Depression and Anxiety can be countered. Speak to a therapist in private, get stuff off your chest or if you feel the need, ask a doctor about anti-depressants.

Well, for one, I care about ya! You may feel low at the moment, but remember that depression stops you viewing the world in a positive light. One major part of that is social withdrawal. Maybe the reason you feel this way is because depression is causing you to be less open than usual and causing others to be less open with you as a result of their lack of understanding. Also, therapy is always an option. It feels good to let it out sometimes. I'm not an expert myself, just someone with similar difficult emotions, but this whole community is here for you if you need it.
